collectionMethod: Manual capture of the official Command Code GOAT pages (English) around 10:30 Beijing time / 02:30Z on 2026-11-13: the GOAT plan page, the public pricing page and the pricing-limits resource page, read as published, and compared line-by-line against the same three pages captured on 2026-11-12. Both the rendered text diff and the embedded RSC payload diff (budgetUsd / rates / budgetSteps / shape / timeOfDay per model) were checked. Research-only — no adopted row generated, no adopted value changed, no script changed.
scope: Command Code GOAT official pages only. One per-model allowance change observed: a new boosted-credits deal for GLM-5.3 (model id 'glm-5.3', provider Z.ai, category opensource, 1M context), whose GOAT per-model monthly credits went from $20 to $70 on the GOAT plan (Pro $30 -> $80, Go unchanged at $10). The three-part price is unchanged (input $1.40 / output $4.40 / cached read $0.26 per 1M tokens, no cache-write price), the GOAT plan-page RSC budgetUsd moved 20 -> 70 with rates, budgetSteps (null), request shape and timeOfDay (null) untouched, and a new 'GLM-5.3 Boosted credits' deal card appeared on the pricing-limits page. The GOAT plan page's official request estimates for GLM-5.3 moved 271 / 677 / 1,350 -> 947 / 2,370 / 4,740 and the credits column moved '$20' -> '$70'. The /pricing page does not list GLM-5.3 separately and did not change. Of the 62 paid models in the GOAT plan-page RSC payload, only glm-5.3 changed budgetUsd. Additionally a new free model 'Inkling 2 Small' appeared, the GOAT model counters moved, the plan page dropped its Intelligence score column, and the GOAT shared-pool wording stayed 'Up to $100'. No leaderboard/score data, no shared-pool change, no other GOAT row changes, no adopted.csv row.

computationNote: No monthlyYi, no blended per-MTok price, no effective min() value, no request count and no adopted value are computed in this file; all dollar figures, request estimates and counters are transcribed as published on the official pages.
confidenceNote: The allowance figures, the RSC payload values and the request estimates are official and internally consistent across the three pages. Confidence is not 'high' because the new GLM-5.3 deal card states no term and no end date: it cannot be determined from the captured pages whether the $70 boost is permanent or merely of unstated duration.
